messages:
deploy-bot: Automated compliance check failed for release candidate rc-4 (tag: r-2026.03.20-rc4). Vulnerability scan flagged CVE-2026-0456 (HIGH) in transitive dependency libfastcodec@2.1.3. Additionally SBOM checksum mismatch for artifact 'service-x:2026.03.20-rc4'. Promotion to canary blocked. Pipeline: https://ci.internal/runs/7890 :warning:

emma: Ack. Is the vuln reproducible locally? who can paste the vuln details? :eyes:

alex: I pulled the SBOM and traced the chain: image-builder@1.0.0 -> thirdparty-parser@0.9.7 -> libfastcodec@2.1.3. Upstream released 2.1.4 with a patch for CVE-2026-0456. The SBOM checksum mismatch looks like the built image included a slightly different thirdparty layer; need to rebuild to be sure.

maria: @alex can we pin to 2.1.4 and re-run SBOM scan? what's the likely hit to our change-window timeline?

sre-oncall: Pin + rebuild will add ~45m for build+CI. Our change window opens in 30m and is 2h long. If the rebuild finishes inside the window we're good, otherwise we risk delaying to next window. Another option: scoped canary to a single region to reduce blast radius.

alex: Bumping image-builder to 1.0.1 (which pins libfastcodec@2.1.4) is the clean fix. I can open a PR to rebuild images and push a new tag. If CI passes we can re-run the SBOM rescan.

emma: Alternative: apply a runtime toggle to disable the vulnerable codepath (mitigation flag). That'd be faster (<15m) but it's an exception and needs stern testing.

legal: If we take an exception (toggle) we need an audit entry, signed justification, and a timeline for permanent remediation. Document exploitability and why it's acceptable as temporary mitigation.

maria: Decision options:
1) rollback rc-4 (revert) and delay release
2) pin+rebuild and retry (delay ~45m)
3) scoped canary (non-global) to keep momentum
4) mitigation toggle with followup patch and audit
Which do we prefer for minimal customer impact?

alex: I prefer pin+rebuild. I'll open PR now, kick CI. If CI green, can deploybot queue the rebuild pipeline and resume canary. If CI fails, fallback to revert.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for PR #3421: https://ci.internal/runs/7890. SBOM rescanner queued. ETA ~35m.

emma: :thumbsup: Alex start the PR. SRE, monitor the CI. If rebuild completes quickly, proceed; otherwise we revert.

maria: I'll prep release note text: "Canary delayed due to third-party vulnerability; patched build being prepared." PMs notified.

sre-oncall: I'll watch metrics and escalate infra if build times spike. If rebuild >90m we postpone to next window.

alex: PR #3421 created, bump image-builder to v1.0.1 and pin libfastcodec@2.1.4. Patch diff snippet:

```diff
- image-builder: 1.0.0
+ image-builder: 1.0.1
- thirdparty-parser: 0.9.7
+ thirdparty-parser: 0.9.8
+ pinned: libfastcodec@2.1.4
```

deploy-bot: SBOM rescanner completed. New image candidate 'service-x:2026.03.20-rc4-patch' checksum now matches expected manifest. Vulnerability status: CVE-2026-0456 -> fixed in candidate image. Full logs: https://ci.internal/logs/7890

maria: OK let's do a targeted canary to us-east-1 only. @sre-oncall please start canary rollout for that region.

sre-oncall: Initiating canary deploy to us-east-1 now. Observability hooks enabled, smoke tests queued. :rocket:

emma: Adding post-deploy smoke: small synthetic workload, token generation correctness, and latency check.

legal: Please attach remediation ticket and timeline for full vendor confirmation. We'll need the audit note in the security folder.

alex: Will open follow-up ticket to track vendor confirmation and CVE closure. Ticket #4529 created.

deploy-bot: Canary finished for us-east-1: no regressions detected by smoke tests. Promotion to global rollout scheduled +1h unless issues reported.

maria: Thanks everyone. Closing this hold for now. Update the release notes with CVE-2026-0456, the mitigation steps taken, and planned followups.

emma: Noting for postmortem: speed up our SBOM parity checks in CI to detect transitive mismatches earlier.

sre-oncall: I'll keep watch for next hour and mark rollback if any anomalies. :white_check_mark:
